startup-em.title: How do you thrive in a startup environment? How do you need to adapt as an EM to be effective at a startup?
lines: What a startup environment means to me, and why I do my best work in it
A concrete example: EarlyDay, from team of one to shipping weekly
How the EM role changes: hands on the code, closer to customers, fewer layers
What I deliberately stop doing compared with a larger company
Close: how I'd adapt specifically for your stage

team-relationship.title: Describe your most effective relationship with the team from a technical perspective. What role do you play? What are you accountable for and what is the team accountable for?
lines: The team I worked best with, and what made it work
The role I play technically: architecture partner, reviewer, unblocker
What I'm accountable for: direction, quality bar, delivery, people
What the team is accountable for: design decisions, estimates, owning production
Where the line moves as the team matures

execution-systems.title: What strategies, processes, and methodologies do you operationalize to get your teams to execute most effectively?
lines: My principle: the lightest process that keeps the team shipping
Planning: outcome-based goals, small batches, weekly priorities
Execution: design docs for big bets, trunk-based delivery, clear ownership
Feedback loops: metrics we actually watch, retros that change things
An example of a process I removed because it slowed us down

hiring-onboarding.title: Describe your experience with the end-to-end process of hiring and onboarding engineers. Where do you have experience being hands-on throughout this process?
lines: How many engineers I've hired, and at what stages
Sourcing and writing the role: where I'm hands on
Interview loop design, rubrics and calibrated debriefs
Closing candidates and selling the mission
Onboarding: first PR in week one, a 30/60/90 plan, a buddy

ai-philosophy.title: Describe your philosophy around, and experience with, AI technologies and tools. How have you personally leveraged these tools and what have you built? How have your teams used them?
lines: My philosophy: AI as leverage for engineers, with evaluation before hype
What I've built personally: agentic pipelines, RAG, AI phone bots at Haestus
How my teams use it day to day: coding agents, review, testing, docs
Results: what got faster, and what we learned not to delegate
Where I think it's heading for engineering teams
